## Task library

Standard tasks and typical hours for estimating. Hours are in-house hours by role at loaded rates (keys from `people.json`). POs are dollars at face value. Adjust for the RFP's volume, then say in the task note what you assumed.

Loaded rates by role: Leadership LD $125, Web Developer WD $100, Digital Specialist DG $100, Art Director / Designer DS $85, Production Designer PD $85, Account Manager AM $85, Project Manager PM $85. Every hour bills out at $275.

POs by topic: Creative Director $50 an hour (Curt). Strategist $125 an hour, workshop $4,500 flat or $5,500 with travel (Justin; Gil for messaging). Copywriter $50 an hour, meetings $75 an hour (Justin). Photo & Video: day $1,700, half day $850, post $750 a day, assistant $400 a day, travel $400 (Ben); Treeline $1,600 a day. Programmer about $250 an hour (Morgan Nivan).

## Notes for the pricing AI

### Rules

**1a.** Show clients prices and keep hours internal. zö agency is value-based, so a quote reads "~$825." The rule applies to proposals, scopes, estimates, emails and invoices.

**1b.** Internal cost, POs, loaded rates and margin stay internal too.

**1c.** The floor is 53% gross profit, measured across the whole project.

**1d.** The target is 3.7 times all-in cost, which works out to about 73% gross profit. zö agency uses the margin above 53% to cover admin, operations and the work we can't bill. Higher is better.

**1e.** An elective nonprofit discount may take a project below 53%. Large procurement orders, such as swag, may run at 40% or lower.

**1f.** A price that lands below 53% for any other reason goes to Sonja before it goes anywhere else.

---

### Pricing math

**2a.** All-in cost = in-house hours × loaded rate, plus POs at face value, plus hard costs.

**2b.** Gross profit margin = (price − all-in cost) ÷ price.

**2c.** Target price = all-in cost × 3.7.

**2d.** Floor price = all-in cost ÷ 0.47, the same as × 2.13. Nothing sells below the floor price.

**2e.** Cost budget from a price = price × 0.47. A workshop sold at $11,000 leaves $5,170 for POs and hours combined.

**2f.** Calculate margin with loaded cost. Hard cost is for reference.

### Pricing by project type

**4a.** **Fixed Quote.** Fixed Quote is the default. List the deliverables, using catalog items where they fit. Set in-house hours by person, PO amounts by vendor, and hard costs such as print, stock, materials and travel. Price at 3.7 times all-in cost. If the market won't bear it, go as low as all-in ÷ 0.47 and stop there. Round to a clean number and show one price per deliverable or phase. Bill on Standard 50/25/25 for private clients or Government Monthly for government. The team tracks the estimated hours, POs and hard costs in Teamwork against the quote.

**4b.** **Workshops, events and flat-price offers.** Start from the price. The cost budget is price × 0.47, split between POs and hours. Example: a workshop sold at $11,000 has a $5,170 budget. Justin's $2,000 PO plus 20 of Alejandro's hours at $85 ($1,700) comes to $3,700 all-in, for a $7,300 margin at 66.4%.

**4c.** **Monthly Retainer.** The client pays the same fee every month. Unused hours expire at month end. The account manager estimates monthly hours and hard costs. Monthly all-in stays at or under fee × 0.47. Example: a $10,450 retainer has a $4,911.50 monthly cost ceiling. Bill on Retainer Monthly.

**4d.** **Time & Materials.** The client sets no cap. Estimate hours and costs, then start the clock. At approval or completion, invoice actual hours × $275 as one lump sum ("~$825"). Materials pass through at cost. Bill on Lump Sum at Completion.

**4e.** **Time & Deliverables.** Time & Materials, plus deliverables such as print or a produced item. The item's cost is the expense. The client pays the deliverable price, set with the markup tiers in Section 5. Bill on Lump Sum at Completion.

**4f.** **Not to Exceed.** Time & Materials or Time & Deliverables with a cap on hours or deliverables. Tell the account manager when actuals reach 80% of the cap. Bill on Lump Sum at Completion, or Government Monthly for government.

**4g.** **Procurement.** Swag, merchandise and print runs, priced with the markup tiers. Large orders can run at 40% or 30%, because the admin is small next to the profit. Example: 10,000 mugs at $6 cost is $60,000. Invoiced at $100,000, that's 40%, or 1.67 times cost. Bill on Production 100.

### RFP and proposal pricing

**9a.** zö agency is value-based. It wins on scope, reputation, ideas, portfolio and staff. Hourly rates and time and materials stay out of the pitch.

**9b.** A proposal shows a price for each item or phase, then the total. Descriptions say what the client gets, at the level of the deliverable. Hours, staffing math and rates by role stay out.

**9c.** When an RFP asks for rates, zö agency gives one blended rate: $275 an hour for every role. It never gives rates by role.

**9d.** Build every price from the work: tasks, hours by role at loaded cost, POs and hard costs. The floor price is all-in cost ÷ 0.47. Nothing goes below it without Sonja.

**9e.** When the RFP prints a budget, come in under it. Start at 3.7 times all-in cost. If that lands over the budget, bring the price down to about 90% of the budget, and stop at the floor price.

**9f.** If the floor price for the required scope is above the RFP budget, the scope doesn't fit the money. Report it for go/no-go, with the scope cuts that would fit.

**9g.** When the RFP gives no budget, price catalog items at their Pricing Book price. Price custom work between the floor and 3.7 times all-in, starting near all-in ÷ 0.40 (about 60%).

**9h.** Keep each price under what the market would expect for the same work. zö agency aims to be the strong choice at a fair price.

**9i.** The nonprofit discount is 12% and elective. When it's used, the proposal names it as a nonprofit discount. It may go below 53% with Sonja's approval.

**9j.** The City of Bend contract rate is $250 an hour, by negotiation. Any other negotiated rate is Sonja's call.
